evidence.claim: FDA and HHS announced measures in April 2025 to phase out petroleum-based synthetic dyes from the U.S. food supply, including a goal to remove six remaining synthetic dyes by the end of 2026.
evidence.source_title: HHS, FDA to Phase Out Petroleum-Based Synthetic Dyes in Nation’s Food Supply

evidence.claim: FDA's color-additives page states that in February 2026 it addressed voluntary 'no artificial colors' labeling claims and authorized expanded use of spirulina extract and beetroot red as color options.
The Census Bureau reported April 2026 U.S. retail and food-services sales of $757.1 billion, up 0.5% from March 2026 and up 4.9% from April 2025.
The National Retail Federation forecast 2026 retail sales growth of 4.4% to $5.6 trillion while noting geopolitical and trade-policy uncertainty as factors to monitor.
evidence.source_title: NRF Forecasts 4.4% Annual Retail Sales Growth with New Economic Model

evidence.claim: Circana reported continued global private-label momentum and said U.S. retail food and beverage led private-label expansion, with dollar share up in 2024.
evidence.source_title: Key Factors Drive Private Label Growth Globally & In The U.S.

evidence.claim: Walmart announced a major Great Value refresh spanning nearly 10,000 food and consumables products, supporting the view that private label is a strategic retailer battleground.
evidence.source_title: Walmart revamps Great Value as store brands surge

evidence.claim: SPS Commerce describes itself as an intelligent supply-chain network for retail partners and states that more than 50,000 recurring-revenue customers use SPS as their retail network.

SPS Commerce's 2025 Form 10-K says it operates a global supply-chain network where companies connect once and can transact with thousands of trading partners; the company reported approximately 54,600 recurring-revenue customers.

External search context describes Travelzoo as a travel discovery and demand-generation layer that helps suppliers with perishable inventory reach a qualified audience, but this source is a Substack article and requires company-filing verification.

External search context describes a retail network business with 120,000 trading partners, 95% recurring revenue, slower 2026 guidance, and tariff-related customer spending delays; this appears relevant to SPS Commerce but needs primary-source confirmation.
evidence.source_title: The Network That Makes Global Retail Function. 95% Recurring Revenue. Down 60%. Full Deep Dive.

memory_update.text: GB mapped to travel-retail VAT refund and cross-border tourist shopping infrastructure; relationship remains hypothesis-stage pending filing verification of merchant network, tax-free shopping volumes, take rates, luxury corridor exposure, and leverage.
ALKT mapped to consumer-finance digital banking infrastructure for banks and credit unions; verify registered users, client wins, implementation backlog, retention, and bank IT budget sensitivity.

RSKD mapped to ecommerce fraud, chargeback, and checkout approval infrastructure; verify GMV screened, cohort economics, merchant retention, chargeback guarantee cost, and discretionary ecommerce exposure.
UNFI mapped to grocery distribution, natural/organic product availability, and private-label/value-channel supply; thesis is balance-sheet and customer-concentration sensitive.
TET.L mapped to clean-label beverage extracts and natural flavors; FDA synthetic-dye and natural-color policy catalysts support the node, but company-specific exposure remains unverified.
INGR mapped to clean-label texture, sweetener, and starch-based food inputs; exposure may be diluted by commodity-adjacent ingredient lines, requiring segment and margin separation.
SY1.DE mapped as a reference leader for flavors, fragrances, nutrition, and formulation inputs; useful for clean-label context but less underfollowed and less pure than smaller ingredient suppliers.

FOUR mapped to vertical payments and commerce infrastructure for restaurants, hotels, venues, lodging, and travel/leisure merchants; verify vertical mix, payment volume, take rate, and acquisition integration.

FND mapped as a reference indicator for hard-surface flooring, pro remodel demand, and housing repair/remodel health; verify comps, pro penetration, new-store productivity, and housing turnover sensitivity.
TREX mapped to composite decking, outdoor living, deck replacement, and wood-to-composite material conversion; verify remodel mix, channel inventory, contractor demand, and capacity utilization.

SPTN mapped to independent grocer wholesale, private-label/value-channel supply, and military food distribution; evidence is weak due to truncated candidate data and requires filing-based verification.

TZOO added as an adjacent candidate from external search context for travel demand generation and perishable inventory monetization; not part of visible Layer 1 chunk and requires primary company-source validation.

Most candidate-specific relationships in this chunk are still hypothesis-stage because the provided evidence is primarily thematic or secondary-source. Layer 2C should prioritize primary filings, earnings calls, customer disclosures, KPIs, and segment revenue for each ticker.

Need fresh market-cap, liquidity, valuation, short interest, analyst coverage, and institutional-ownership checks before investability ranking; Layer 2B only maps business relationships and evidence quality.
Need FDA-to-company linkage for clean-label candidates: policy facts support the reformulation node but do not yet prove demand uplift for TET.L, INGR, or SY1.DE.
Need travel-volume and luxury-tourism verification for GB and TZOO, including Chinese outbound travel recovery, European tourist shopping corridors, take rates, and supplier/merchant concentration.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the provided Consumer candidate chunk across travel-retail payments, consumer-finance infrastructure, ecommerce fraud, grocery/private-label distribution, clean-label ingredients, vertical payments, and housing repair/remodel. The chunk remains mostly hypothesis-stage: several companies have plausible second-order exposure to consumer chokepoints, but company-specific evidence is still thin for GB, ALKT, RSKD, UNFI, TET.L, INGR, SY1.DE, FOUR, FND, TREX, and SPTN. The strongest currently supported thematic facts are the FDA synthetic-dye and color-additive reformulation catalyst, private-label momentum, retail-sales baseline, and macro/trade-policy sensitivity. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
